newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas extends losses on weather, futures.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas extends losses on weather, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to soften Tuesday as forecasts called for moderate weather throughout most of the U.S. this week and gas futures faltered, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices fell eight to nine cents to about $2.05-2.10 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $2.07-2.14 and Transco (Station 65) pegged around $2.08-2.09.
NYMEX's July Henry Hub gas futures early in the session dropped to a low of $2.08 per mmBtu, down three cents from Monday.

Temperatures throughout most of the East, upper Midwest and Northwest are forecast to hover below normal this week, with the Southwest expected to experience slightly cooler weather later in the week.

In Phoenix, temperature highs are expected to remain above 100 degrees F through Thursday, while temperatures in Los Angeles are forecast to hit highs in the mid-to-high 70s Wednesday and Thursday, Weather Services Corp said.
As a result of the cooler weather in southern California, Permian prices slipped nine cents to the mid-$1.90s, while Southern California border prices were quoted mostly at $2.13-2.14.
In the Midwest, where warmer air is expected to arrive this weekend, prices drifted five cents lower to about $2.
Chicago city-gate prices were talked around $2.20.

Meanwhile in the East, New York city gate prices lost about five to 10 cents to $2.35-2.40 as cool, rainy weather provided no air conditioning demand for the area. Although temperatures are expected to moderate gradually this week, weather is still forecast to remain cooler than normal through the weekend, according to WSC.
